entries.reason: iOS 9 gave the creation request its own subclass so a resource can be attached before the write; iOS 6 still has only ALAssetsLibrary's single write to the saved photos, so the resource is staged and written at commit the same way PHAssetChangeRequest's own creation request is
entries.effect: +creationRequestForAsset opens a request; addResourceWithType:data:options: and addResourceWithType:fileURL:options: accept exactly one photo or video resource (a second call, or any other resource type, fails the change); +supportsAssetResourceTypes: answers YES only for a single photo or video type; placeholderForCreatedAsset resolves like PHAssetChangeRequest's
entries.source: the header of iOS 16.4 for the declarations; verified against this port's own PHAssetChangeRequest (facts/Photos/Changes.md), which PHAssetCreationRequest inherits from in the SDK; a video as a file, moved or not, and as data in a QuickTime and an MPEG-4 container, run on an iPad 2 running 6.1.3 with tests/backports/device/photosdata9.m on 2026-09-24, 34 checks, 0 failures (one, the replacement of a file already there, since dropped)

entries.reason: the options object is plain state (a filename, a UTI, whether to move the file); ALAssetsLibrary's write always copies, so a move is that copy followed by the removal of the file
entries.effect: originalFilename, uniformTypeIdentifier and shouldMoveFile are held and copied; shouldMoveFile on a file resource removes the file once the asset is made, refuses a hard-linked file or one whose folder does not let it be removed with PHPhotosErrorInvalidResource before anything is written, and fails the change with the file system's error if the removal fails after the write
entries.source: the header of iOS 16.4 for the declarations; shouldMoveFile on a file, moved, kept and refused for a hard-linked file, run on an iPad 2 running 6.1.3 with tests/backports/device/photosdata9.m on 2026-09-24, 34 checks, 0 failures (one, the replacement of a file already there, since dropped)

entries.reason: iOS 6 has one resource per asset, the primary representation ALAssetsLibrary gives, so the class describes that representation rather than a Photos database row
entries.effect: +assetResourcesForAsset: gives one PHAssetResource built from the asset's defaultRepresentation (type, UTI and filename); +assetResourcesForLivePhoto: always gives an empty array, since iOS 6 has no live photos
entries.source: the header of iOS 16.4 for the declarations; ALAssetRepresentation of an iPad 2 running 6.1.3 for the shape of a representation; the resource list of a live photo not yet measured, since no live photo can exist on this release

entries.reason: the options object is plain state (whether the network may be used, a progress block); iOS 6 always reads the asset from local storage, so networkAccessAllowed changes nothing, and progress is the part of the representation read so far
entries.effect: networkAccessAllowed is held and copied but not read back, since ALAssetsLibrary never reaches the network for a local asset's bytes; progressHandler is called after each chunk the read hands over, with the part read so far, the last time with 1.0
entries.source: the header of iOS 16.4 for the declarations; the progress handler, once per chunk and ending at 1.0, run on an iPad 2 running 6.1.3 with tests/backports/device/photosdata9.m on 2026-09-24, 34 checks, 0 failures (one, the replacement of a file already there, since dropped); networkAccessAllowed is held and has no network to allow on this release

entries.reason: the manager gives back the bytes of the one resource an iOS 6 asset has; it reads them from the same ALAssetRepresentation that PHAssetResource itself was built from
entries.effect: +defaultManager gives one shared instance; requestDataForAssetResource:options:dataReceivedHandler:completionHandler: reads the representation one chunk at a time and hands each chunk to dataReceivedHandler, then calls completionHandler with nil, or with an error and no further chunk if the asset is gone (PHPhotosErrorIdentifierNotFound), has no representation (PHPhotosErrorMissingResource) or the release gives no more bytes before the representation's own size; writeDataForAssetResource:toFile:options:completionHandler: writes the chunks as they are read into a file beside the given one and renames it into place when all are in, leaving the given file as it was on a failure (a file already there is replaced on success: the port's choice, what Photos does there is not measured); cancelDataRequest: stops a request before its next chunk and makes it call completionHandler once, with PHPhotosErrorUserCancelled; a completed request is not changed
entries.source: the header of iOS 16.4 for the declarations; verified against this port's own PHAssetResource and ALAssetRepresentation.getBytes:fromOffset:length:error:; the chunked read, its cancel and the write to a file held to a direct ALAssetsLibrary read of the same asset, run on an iPad 2 running 6.1.3 with tests/backports/device/photosdata9.m on 2026-09-24, 34 checks, 0 failures (one, the replacement of a file already there, since dropped)
